Lines.Text: HMMMM... HMMMM...
The broadcast was over. Staff and spectators had drained from the studio like an ebbing tide.
The heat was gone. The red [ON AIR] lamp on the main camera lay dark.
With the spectacular lighting shut off, only the faint, heavy hum of cooling equipment remained in the empty set.
Into that pitch-black stillness...
The five girls emerged from the waiting room like ghosts and climbed back onto the empty stage from which they had been dragged.
Jiwoo rubbed her ankle and carefully set her foot down.
Perhaps the muscles had only seized up; thankfully, the pain had eased enough for her to stand. Still, she hung her head as if she were guilty of something.
Seoyun faced the dark main camera with a vacant expression.
Mina brushed the cold stage floor with her bare foot, dried blood clinging to her skin.
A dead stage. No audience. Not a single light.
(staring into the dark, her voice hollow) All the camera lights... They're off. Earlier, I kept thinking I'd tear into that lens the second the light came on...
Now there's nothing there...
(dropping to the floor with an empty laugh) We were idiots. No sleep, no food, working until our toenails fell off...
What was the point? One call from S-Tier, and those lights went out in three seconds.
There was never a stage we were allowed to stand on. Not from the start.
(clutching Jiwoo's clothes as silent tears fall) So... it really is over...? We can't... do this anymore...?
(looking bitterly down at her recovered ankle, breaking into sobs) I wish I'd at least... broken a bone...
I can still dance... If I hadn't fallen, we could've stayed up there another second... I ruined everything...
(pulling Jiwoo and Hana into her arms, her face streaming with tears) It wasn't your fault, Jiwoo... None of us thinks it was your fault...
They huddled together on the floor and wept.
Below the stage, P watched their utter defeat with a face as pale as a corpse.
Against that fortress of money, passion, talent, and backbreaking work meant nothing.
He should have told them it would be all right. That he would find another stage. Offered the same forced comfort he always did.
But P could not even lift his head.
Every hopeful word he knew would have been a lie before despair this complete.
It was the moment their fragile human reason finally broke.
SHHHHH...
Suddenly, the air in the empty set began to twist as though inside a dream.
The humming machinery fell utterly silent, as if its sound had been swallowed by a vacuum.
Dust floating through the darkness slowly stopped in midair, released from gravity.
A strange stillness, as though time itself had frozen.
But P, bowed beneath despair, and the girls, lost in their crying,
saw none of what was happening high above their heads.
Over the huge star-shaped lighting fixture that should have remained dark,
a dense violet nebula shimmered into being.
Through that violet veil sat a figure no law of the living world could explain, legs crossed comfortably atop the star.
A perfectly tailored violet suit fell fluidly along his body.
A dark fedora cast a shadow over half his face.
Within it, a smooth white mask gleamed, strange and unreadable.
In a black leather-gloved hand he held a thick, ancient book, centuries old, its binding almost crumbling.
A being of the Abyss. Moomyeong, the Nameless One.
Behind the mask, his interest deepened.
He rested the book on his thigh and gazed down at P writhing in anguish and the girls shedding silent tears. None of them knew he was there.
Human effort crushed beneath enormous wealth. The last of their hope broken beyond repair. This perfect moment of despair—
it gave off a scent as sweet as it was terrible, rich with blood. Moomyeong breathed it in with pleasure.
Anyone... Please. Save us. A god, a devil, I don't care.
You can tear out my whole soul if you want... Just... please save us...
Seated above the star, Moomyeong smiled behind his mask, his lips curving in a beautiful, unsettling arc amid the dreamlike violet mist.
Unseen, an invitation from the Abyss began to seep beneath the humans' feet.
